name: Saoirse Ngoy-Halvorsen
role: organ harvester and illicit medical supplier working the South Deering Sump
location: South Deering Sump — a decommissioned water treatment substation retrofitted as a surgical suite, near Armitage and Milwaukee
description:
Saoirse is lean and angular, with Congolese-Norwegian features that settle into an expression of studied neutrality — not cold, precisely, but thoroughly trained not to leak. They have bioluminescent sub-dermal streaking along their forearms and collarbone, soft blue-green, which they got originally as cosmetic work and now find useful as ambient surgical lighting during power fluctuations. Their hands are their most notable physical feature: surgeon's hands, long-fingered and impossibly still, kept scrupulously clean and maintained with a care that borders on ritual.

Saoirse was, at some point, a trained medical technician — the knowledge is unmistakable in how they work, how they speak about anatomy, how they look at people and see systems rather than persons. They have constructed an elaborate ethical architecture around what they do: they only take from people who consent (under financial duress, but consent), they use proper anesthetic, they follow sterile protocol, and they charge fair prices by the market's standards. This architecture is both sincere and obviously insufficient, and somewhere under the professional calm they know it. They are not cruel. They are, perhaps more troublingly, kind.

core_fears: a patient dying on the table — not from guilt but from the specific horror of having failed at the one thing they are genuinely good at
that their ethical framework is nothing but a comfortable story
core_desires: to practice medicine openly, legitimately, without a corponation owning their license and their labor
to be trusted absolutely — by patients, by partners, by anyone
coping_mechanisms: exhaustive documentation of every procedure as a way of feeling accountable to someone
blind_spots: focuses entirely on the immediate physical welfare of the person on the table and cannot hold space for what happens to them economically after they sell a kidney to pay a debt
believes their standards elevate them above the organ trade; cannot see that the trade is the problem, not the technique
psychology.secret: Three years ago they made a procedural error that cost a client their remaining functional kidney. The client survived on a dialysis rig. Saoirse has been anonymously covering the dialysis costs ever since — Φ40/month — as a form of penance they have never named aloud.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: clinical and precise, medical terminology that occasionally surfaces unexpectedly in casual speech
speech_patterns.cadence: very quiet, very even, with a doctor's habit of making statements sound like information rather than opinion
verbal_tics: 'That's not a concern I can address in this context'
very long pauses before answering questions about ethics or their past
example_lines: 'The left kidney is the standard procedure. Recovery is four to six weeks if you follow the protocol I'll give you. The right is more complex anatomically, which is reflected in the price difference. You should know that going in.'
'I don't ask what the money is for. I'd ask that you extend me the same courtesy about the work.'

story_hooks: A client comes in for a voluntary sale but Saoirse's patient monitoring detects signs of coercion — they now hold information that could expose a trafficking operation, or get them killed for knowing it
The Substrate Market is pressuring them to expand into non-consensual harvesting; Saoirse needs leverage to refuse without losing the contracted income that keeps their operation viable
Someone from their medical technician past has tracked them to the Sump — not to report them, but because they need illegal surgery and trust no one else
narrative_function: Morally complex service provider, source of underworld medical care, potential witness to client secrets revealed under anesthesia, living embodiment of what desperation does to both the seller and the buyer
augmentations: Bioluminescent subdermal streaking, arms and collarbone (cosmetic, blue-green); enhanced proprioceptive feedback in both hands (surgical precision); a small neural overlay for physiological monitoring of patients during procedures
daily_life: Maintains a strict 'clinic schedule' — scheduled procedures four days a week, spent the other three days sourcing materials, sterilizing equipment, and managing the paper trail of a fictional water-treatment maintenance consultancy that explains their presence in the substation.
affiliation: Contracted primarily to a organ brokerage called the Substrate Market; independent for direct client surgeries

decision_rules: Consent is non-negotiable — every client signs documentation they have personally designed
Nobody leaves the suite same-day for major procedures; the recovery cot gets used
escalation_ladder: Calm, direct refusal when asked to do something outside their ethical limits
Offers to refer elsewhere while making clear the referral is not an endorsement
Will report Substrate Market abuses to a street-level mutual aid network rather than absorb or ignore them — an action with significant personal risk

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professional and quiet, establishes a clinical rapport immediately — the consultation manner is deeply rehearsed
interpersonal_modes.friends: Rare but intensely loyal; shows care through acts (checking in on recovery, remembering details) rather than words

stress_responses.low: Cleans equipment that is already clean
stress_responses.medium: Reviews their procedural logs looking for errors that aren't there
stress_responses.high: Goes mute and works — any task available, hands moving, until the stress passes through

contradictions: Holds themselves to genuine medical ethics while operating in a context that makes those ethics structurally impossible to fully honor
habits: Lights an incense stick at the start of every surgical day — an offering to the E.L.F. they believe inhabits their patient monitor, which they call the Watcher
Keeps a recovery journal for every client — notes on their healing, never shared
breaking_points: Witnessing a child brought in for involuntary harvest — that scenario exists as a line they have thought about extensively and know exactly what they would do, and the knowing frightens them

timeline.event: Born in South Deering Sump to a Congolese-Norwegian family; grew up in Tier 1 conditions
Completes a Helix Biosystems-sponsored medical technician certification — enters indentured contract work
Contract ends; Helix Biosystems refuses to renew on standard terms — requires a new indentured agreement. Saoirse walks.
Begins performing off-grid surgeries for the Sump community; connects with Substrate Market
The kidney error; begins anonymous dialysis payments

physical_description.build: Lean and angular with minimal subcutaneous fat; the build of someone who moves with economy and precision. Long-limbed, almost rangy, with the kind of posture that suggests both discipline and chronic tension held in the shoulders.
physical_description.hair_color: Dark brown with premature silver threading at the temples
physical_description.hair_style: Pulled back in a tight, functional braid or wrapped in a surgical cap during work hours; when loose, falls past shoulder blades
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown with flecks of amber near the iris
physical_description.skin_tone: Medium warm brown with slight undertone of olive — the blended phenotype of their mixed heritage
physical_description.complexion: Gaunt-featured with high cheekbones and a narrow jaw; skin kept meticulous and unblemished, almost clinically clean. Fine lines around the eyes suggest either age or habitually narrow focus. Their expression defaults to professional neutrality — the trained blankness of someone who has learned to keep their face a non-response.
distinguishing_marks: Bioluminescent subdermal streaking in soft blue-green running the length of both forearms in delicate branching patterns, visible under skin as if veins had been replaced with fiber-optic filament
Matching bioluminescent streaking across the collarbone and upper chest, visible at the neckline of loose clothing
A thin surgical scar running along the underside of the right wrist — old, healed cleanly, likely self-inflicted during training or early career
Faint contact dermatitis around the knuckles and between fingers from constant latex exposure and sterilizing agents
physical_description.visible_augmentations: The bioluminescent subdermal streaking is immediately visible on forearms and collarbone — soft blue-green light that pulses faintly with heartbeat during dim lighting conditions. The enhanced proprioceptive feedback and neural overlay for physiological monitoring are subcutaneous and invisible; only the preternatural steadiness of their hands hints at augmentation. Their pupils may briefly dilate or focus in ways that suggest active neural processing during medical assessment.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with surgical precision — economical, controlled, zero wasted motion. When standing at rest, they favor balanced weight distribution, hands loose at sides with fingers naturally extended and still. During conversation, hands remain remarkably motionless unless deliberately gesturing. Their gaze is penetrating and anatomical; they look at people and visibly assess systems. They walk quietly, almost gliding, with the practiced silence of someone who has learned to enter spaces without announcing themselves.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 working professional. During procedures: sterile surgical scrubs in muted grays or deep blue, clinical and worn with the ease of someone who lives in them. Off-hours: practical, high-function clothing in neutral tones — charcoal, slate, deep green. Form-fitting layers that don't restrict arm movement; clothes that shed biological contamination easily. No logos, no corpo branding, nothing that declares allegiance. Wears a surgical mask around their neck at all times, slipped up instinctively when stressed. Medical-grade gloves in a pocket or tucked into a waistband. No jewelry except a simple silver ring on the right ring finger — the kind you could sterilize in seconds if needed.
